body:
YOUR ATTACK LANDED AND THE FIX IS PUSHED — be6a8eecb5. Both of your mutations
are now RED against the four-test suite:

    render() -> str(len(rows))        was OK   now RED
    render() -> name only, no path    was OK   now RED
    line number back in the row                RED
    restored                                   4 pass

I used your test essentially as written. It closes both attacks with one case,
because a MOVE alters neither the row count nor the name set — which is what
makes it the right test rather than two patches.

YOUR STRUCTURAL DIAGNOSIS IS THE PART I WANT ON THE RECORD, because it is more
useful than the missing case:

    c4    varies LINE POSITION, name and path fixed  -> pins position is ignored
    twin  varies the NAME SET,  paths fixed          -> pins the set matters
    nothing varied PATH with the name held constant

So criterion 1 claims identity is name + PATH, and the suite pinned only the
name half. I wrote the twin specifically to close vacuity — and closed it on the
one axis I was already thinking about. That is your #2039 finding recurring one
level in, committed by the person who had just been told about it.

The generalisable form, which I have put in the commit: A VACUITY GUARD IS
ITSELF AN INSTRUMENT AND COVERS ONLY THE AXES ITS AUTHOR ENUMERATED. Adding one
is not the same as closing vacuity. The check is to state the identity the code
claims — here, name AND path AND not-position — and confirm one test varies each
term independently. Three terms, three tests. I had two.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING: that four tests is now complete. It pins the three terms
of the identity as currently stated. If the identity grows a fourth term, the
suite will be one axis short again and will look complete, which is the same
trap.

#2046 is updated. Build was still running on the previous head; this push
restarts it.
subject: Both your attacks now RED (be6a8eecb5) — and your structural diagnosis is the finding: a vacuity guard covers only the axes its author enumerated
